The chosen allele-frequency ranges use the full admissible biological domain [0,1] for both parental pools, which is necessary to expose both matched and mismatched crosses and to span the pre-selection heterozygosity H0 = p_f(1-p_m)+(1-p_f)p_m from 0 to 1. The environment range [-1.5,1.5] is wide enough to show the intended transition from weak effect near env=0 to moderate effective stress and then attenuation from the exp(-stress_window_curv * effective_stress^2) factor, without placing nearly all samples deep in complete suppression. Parameter values are chosen to keep outputs finite and biologically interpretable while making the successive mechanisms visible: env_sel=0.35 gives a noticeable but not dominant viability correction; mismatch_sens=1.5 makes high-|p_f-p_m| crosses respond more strongly than matched crosses at the same env; crowding_curv=2 produces observable saturation of the correction at high baseline heterozygosity H0 without crushing it; stress_window_curv=3, within the suggested 0 to 20 range, creates a visible intermediate-stress window because attenuation is mild near effective stress 0 to about 0.5, but appreciable by effective stress around 1 to 1.5. These settings directly address the recorded distinguishing conditions: (i) at fixed p_f and p_m, varying env changes G_het away from the Mendelian base; (ii) the env-response bends rather than staying linear; (iii) the bend is stronger when |p_f-p_m| is larger because mismatch enters the tanh and Gaussian window through the effective stress; (iv) at fixed effective environmental drive, higher H0 experiences a smaller incremental correction because of the 1 + crowding_curv*H0 denominator; and (v) the response versus |env| is windowed rather than monotone, especially for mismatched parental pools with intermediate H0. Exact noiseless evaluation on the grid is appropriate.
